statistics.title: Missoula renter cost burden
statistics.description: Renter households paying 30% or more of household income toward housing costs in 2024.

statistics.title: People counted unsheltered
statistics.description: People counted as unsheltered in Missoula during the 2026 Point-in-Time count. A one-night count is a snapshot, not a full annual measure.

statistics.title: Individuals and families secured housing
statistics.description: People and families reported as securing housing through local community efforts; the City notes some moved to permanent rentals and some with family or friends.

progress.title: Affordable homes planned across five Montana communities
progress.description: The Montana Board of Housing allocated federal housing tax credits for 136 affordable homes across five communities. The award includes 30 planned homes at Franklin Crossing in Missoula; these are planned homes, not completed units.

progress.title: A family-focused transition housing program in development
progress.description: Missoula Interfaith Collaborative acquired a property for a planned transitional housing program for families leaving shelter, with behavioral health and addiction-service partnerships. The article described a hoped-for 2027 opening; it is a developing project, not a completed or evaluated outcome.

articles.title: New transitional housing for families in the works
articles.summary: Missoula Interfaith Collaborative purchased a property for a planned transitional housing program for families leaving shelter. The story describes a partnership-based approach intended to combine stable housing with connections to behavioral health, addiction services and other supports.

articles.title: Montana Board of Housing allocates funding to build 136 affordable homes
articles.summary: The state announced federal housing tax-credit allocations supporting 136 affordable homes in five Montana communities. The release identifies 30 planned homes at Franklin Crossing in Missoula; these awards support future development and do not mean the homes are already complete.

articles.title: What Missoula's homelessness response looks like one year after Johnson Street shelter closure
articles.summary: The report looks at how Missoula's response changed after the Johnson Street shelter closed, including pressure on remaining shelter capacity and outreach. It notes that the January Point-in-Time count is a one-night snapshot and may undercount people experiencing homelessness.

articles.title: Survey IDs top barriers for Missoula renters
articles.summary: A Missoula renter survey identified unaffordable rents, income requirements and a shortage of pet-friendly rentals among common housing barriers. The story also reports that more than half of surveyed renters had difficulty finding their current home and 77% searched for at least a month.
